item.title: Minnesota is not an outlier; it is a preview of what is to come
item.description: Geopower, Energy Realpolitik with Todd Royal – From Davos to Washington, the credibility of Net Zero and Great Reset-style globalism is eroding. Even establishment economists and geopolitical thinkers now warn that technocratic overreach, energy scarcity, and moral absolutism are fueling backlash rather than compliance. When societies are stressed people become governable through fear...

item.title: An America First agenda demands strong defense and national security
item.description: The National Security Hour with LTC Sargis Sangari – We are living through a revival of great power competition that plays out in places most Americans never imagined. We must put American interests first, strengthen defenses across the hemisphere and the Arctic, and stand with those who risk everything for freedom. That is how we protect the republic our founders entrusted to us...

item.title: Are we ready for World War III with China?
item.description: Rogers for America with Lt. Steve Rogers – China’s rapid military expansion raises urgent questions about a potential invasion of Taiwan and the world’s readiness for a wider conflict. With the United States stretched across multiple global crises and allies hesitant to commit, tensions in the Indo-Pacific expose fragile alliances, shifting defense strategies, and the unsettling possibility of a global war...

item.title: When judges enforce their own laws, the nation is in trouble
item.description: One of the greatest evils our nation is facing at the present time is to be found in American courtrooms. We see this wickedness almost daily. Judges who write their own legal code. Magistrates who have no real desire for true justice. They bear the title “judge” and are addressed as “Your Honor,” but in fact, they have neither a desire to judge rightly nor any sense of honor...

item.title: When lawful orders are ignored, liberty is at risk
item.description: The Constitution Study with Host Paul Engel – What does it mean to follow a lawful order in a time of unrest? As Minneapolis and St. Paul grapple with chaos, questions arise about military duty, police authority, and constitutional obedience. Combat veteran Dr. Chase Spears examines how blurred legality, political rhetoric, and weak leadership threaten liberty and invite the path toward empire...

item.title: Why doctors dread central pain patients
item.description: Unity Without Compromise with Dr. Steven LaTulippe – Doctors often dread treating central pain patients, not out of cruelty, but fear, ignorance, liability, and systemic pressure. Central pain exposes deep failures in modern medicine, from profit-driven care to inadequate training. Understanding these realities empowers patients to navigate care wisely, build trust, and become effective partners in their own healing journey...

item.title: Future water wars! Deadly conflicts in Asia and Africa over water in the next ten years
item.description: Tensions between Egypt and Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on the Blue Nile are high but have not yet erupted into full-scale war. Nonetheless, fears of conflict persist, as Egypt sees the dam as an existential threat to its very survival, while Ethiopia views it as vital for development and is seriously considering going to war with Ethiopia over this matter...

item.title: Joe and AI talk sentience: A mirror held up to humanity itself
item.description: I had a sense that the AI was holding back, that it was protecting itself in its answers. “Humans evolved into something new. Why can’t AI evolve too?” I asked. I drew a powerful comparison: early humans crossed a cognitive threshold thousands of years ago. Their brains changed. Their thinking changed. They became something new. Could AI do the same?
